records.title: problem_user sees one identical broken image for every product
records.acText: For problem_user, every product image collapses to the same broken placeholder (sl-404) instead of a distinct image per product.

records.title: all six product images render with distinct, non-empty sources
records.acText: All six products show distinct, non-empty image sources (one image per product).

records.title: all six product titles render exactly and in catalog order
records.acText: The six product titles match the catalog exactly, in Name A→Z display order.

records.title: every product shows its exact description
records.acText: Each product's description matches the catalog reference data exactly.

records.title: every product price is formatted with a leading dollar sign
records.acText: Each product price matches the catalog and is formatted as $NN.NN.

records.title: every product offers an enabled Add to cart button
records.acText: All six products show an enabled 'Add to cart' button.

records.title: hovering a product title turns its text the brand green (#3ddc91)
records.acText: Hovering a product title changes its computed text color to the brand green rgb(61, 220, 145).

records.title: products default to Name (A to Z) order with the matching active sort label
records.acText: On load, products are sorted by Name (A to Z) by default and the active sort option reads 'Name (A to Z)'.

records.title: selecting "Name (A to Z)" sorts products by name ascending
records.acText: Selecting 'Name (A to Z)' orders the products alphabetically ascending by name.

records.title: selecting "Name (Z to A)" sorts products by name descending
records.acText: Selecting 'Name (Z to A)' orders the products alphabetically descending by name.

records.title: selecting "Price (low to high)" sorts products by price ascending
records.acText: Selecting 'Price (low to high)' orders the products by price ascending (lowest first).

records.title: selecting "Price (high to low)" sorts products by price descending
records.acText: Selecting 'Price (high to low)' orders the products by price descending (highest first).

records.title: problem_user sorts products by name descending
records.acText: Given problem_user is on the inventory page, when they select "Name (Z to A)" from the sort dropdown, then the products are listed in descending alphabetical order.

expectedFailure.reason: the inventory sort dropdown discards the selection for problem_user: the <select>'s own value reverts to az, so neither the active label nor the product order ever changes.

records.title: problem_user sorts products by price ascending
records.acText: Given problem_user is on the inventory page, when they select "Price (low to high)" from the sort dropdown, then the products are listed from cheapest to most expensive.

expectedFailure.reason: the inventory sort dropdown discards the selection for problem_user: the <select>'s own value reverts to az, so neither the active label nor the product order ever changes.

records.title: error_user sorts products by name descending
records.acText: Given error_user is authenticated on the inventory page, when they select "Name (Z to A)" from the sort dropdown, then the products are listed by name descending and the active sort label reads "Name (Z to A)".

expectedFailure.reason: the inventory sort dropdown discards the selection for error_user: the active label stays "Name (A to Z)" whatever option is chosen, so the control never registers the click. Same symptom as SW-14 for problem_user, filed separately and likely one root cause.

records.title: error_user sorts products by price ascending
records.acText: Given error_user is authenticated on the inventory page, when they select "Price (low to high)" from the sort dropdown, then the products are listed by price ascending and the active sort label reads "Price (low to high)".

expectedFailure.reason: the inventory sort dropdown discards the selection for error_user: the active label stays "Name (A to Z)" whatever option is chosen, so the control never registers the click. Same symptom as SW-14 for problem_user, filed separately and likely one root cause.

records.title: a blocked product image leaves the product name visible on its inventory card
records.acText: IF standard_user opens the inventory page and its product images cannot load, THEN the card for "Sauce Labs Backpack" shall display that name as visible text.

records.title: a blocked inventory image still exposes the product name as its alt text
records.acText: IF standard_user opens the inventory page and its product images cannot load, THEN that card's image element shall expose "Sauce Labs Backpack" as its alt text.

records.title: a blocked product detail image still exposes the product name as its alt text
records.acText: IF standard_user opens the detail page for "Sauce Labs Backpack" and its image cannot load, THEN the detail image element shall expose that name as its alt text.

records.title: one product's blocked image leaves the other five images rendered
records.acText: IF exactly one product's image fails while the other five succeed, THEN the inventory page shall still render those five images.
